diet.text: Mainly crayfish, especially freshly moulted ones

overview.text: Graham's Crayfish Snake is a harmless, semi-aquatic snake of the central United States that eats mainly crayfish.

identification.text: Brown or grey, sometimes with a faint stripe down the middle of the back.

size.label: Adults
size.text: Usually 18 to 28 in (46 to 71 cm); the record is 47 in (119 cm).

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: Arkansas, Illinois, Iowa, Kansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, Missouri, Nebraska, Oklahoma and Texas.

habitat.text: Edges of muddy marshes, oxbow lakes, rivers, streams and roadside ditches full of crayfish; it hides under debris and in crayfish burrows.

diet.text: Mostly crayfish, especially ones that have just moulted; also fish and amphibians.

reproduction.text: Gives birth to 10 to 15 live young, each about 20 cm long.

recognise.text: Plain brown or grey snake near muddy water.
